verdict.rationale: Fly.io's own docs say apps can be deployed in regions worldwide, with users routed to the nearest server over a global Anycast network. Fly Machines are described as running close to users, and multi-region deployment is available with a single command. Community reliability complaints are about outages, not about whether global placement works, so they do not dispute this capability. Missing for 10: independent hands-on corroboration of latency gains from proximity (the one community mention of performance uplift is vague).

support.subject: As a developer, I can run my code on a global edge network close to end users

citations.quote: You can deploy apps in regions worldwide, so your users in Tokyo, São Paulo, or Amsterdam connect to the nearest server through our global Anycast network.
Fly Machines are hardware-isolated VMs that boot in under a second, run close to your users
deploy to those regions with a single command
Fly.io converts Docker images to fast-booting VMs and runs them globally.
